worldMap.label: World map
worldMap.short: The maps of a region side by side, for example Sinnoh; HeartGold and SoulSilver have Johto and Kanto.

area.label: Area
area.short: A piece of a world map with a name, such as a town or a route; areas with a map of their own are listed under “More areas”.

room.label: Room
room.short: Interiors, caves and dungeons; a room belongs to the area where its entrance is.

place.label: Place
place.short: The name the game shows on entering; areas and rooms carry it, several can share the same.

landscape.label: Landscape
landscape.short: The cells of a world map that belong to no area: sea, mountains and edge.

header.label: Header
header.short: An entry of the place table: points to matrix, event file, area data, music and weather. Only in Tinker; Build says area, room or place.

outside.label: Outside
outside.short: A header whose grid has a header section (the region, usually matrix 0): the cells of the grid say which header applies where.

matrix.label: Matrix
matrix.short: A grid of maps, 1 × 1 to 255 × 255. Only in Tinker; Build says world map.

map.label: Map
map.short: 32 × 32 tiles with model, buildings and collision.

warp.label: Entrance / Exit
warp.short: A warp pair connects two places.

eventFile.label: Event file
eventFile.short: Warps, objects, triggers and background events of a place.

textArchive.label: Text archive
textArchive.short: The messages of a place; scripts show them by number.

message.label: Message
message.short: A text of a text archive; scripts fetch it by its number.

scriptFile.label: Script file
scriptFile.short: All scripts of a place in one file; events name the number #n in it.

script.label: Script
script.short: A sequence in rotom, for example script Main #1.

levelScript.label: Level script
levelScript.short: Runs when the map loads or is entered, or when a variable has a value.

problem.label: Problem
problem.short: An error or a warning from compile, text or language service.

patch.label: ROM patch
patch.short: A permanent change to the game code. The “Dynamic Headers” patch moves the headers into one file per header so that new ones can be created; DSPRE knows it.
